references.text: Deals with the right of redemption when an Israelite has sold their property due to poverty, and a relative is to redeem it.
Describes the duty to help a brother who has become poor and lives among you as a foreigner or traveler.
Concerns an Israelite who sells themselves due to poverty but must be treated as a hired worker, not as a slave.
A direct continuation explaining the right of redemption for one who has sold themselves to a foreigner.
Prophetic warning that foreigners will rise above the Israelites if they do not keep the covenant.
Nehemiah criticizes the Jews for selling their brothers, who then must be redeemed again.
The Lord asks rhetorically whom Israel was sold to because of their sins.
Israel was sold for nothing and shall be redeemed without money.
